title.narrative: Kutoka Network: Sauti Kutoka ghetto - Boresha Maisha

description.narrative:
This is a grant that will begin the combination/ intergration of Kutoka network and St. John's Sports society activities that are all under the St. Johns Parish in Korogocho both initiatives are geared towards an integral human development through sports and media. St. John Sports Society is an initiative of St. John's Christian Community which has served communities in Korogocho beyond the spiritual needs over the last 20 years. Korogocho is a low-income, informal settlement with around 100,000 people located in the Kasarani Constituency of East Nairobi and is divided into nine villages inhabited by people from across all Kenyan communities, with most of them living below the poverty line.
Kutoka Network is a voluntary gathering of Catholic Parishes and organisations working and ministering to people living in various Nairobi informal settlements. Founded in 2002, the Network looks at the problems affecting the people in the slums, with the eyes of the Gospel. The aim of the network is to analyse the reality of the slums, to share experiences, to reflect together on the pastoral approach, to plan common initiatives and actions and to highlight positive aspects of the slum realities. Most of the ctions lobby the government and other stakeholders to find together with the slums dwellers the solutions to the problems affecting our communities.
The St. John Sports Society, Korogocho (SSS)'s goal is to promote an integral human development with a focus to developing the sporting potential among the youth and women thereby helping them access opportunities beyond Korogocho. Its main focus is on human formation and community work. Through SSS's formation programmes the members develop certain acceptable ethical and societal norms, and qualities which help them integrate with the whole society without difficulties. Values such as teamwork, tolerance, forgiveness and reconciliation, self-esteem and self-discipline, morality, commitment and hard work, zero tolerance to corruption and discrimination of any form are encouraged and developed during the formation programmes.
The SSS operates on certain lessons learnt in working in the slums of Korogocho. These include, that sports has a potential to rehabilitate youths in a slum setting making them reformed and more productive members of the society; and that the slums have tremendously talented sports men and women who only lack exposure and support.
This phase of the radio programme has been shaped by the findings of the programme impact survey that recommended the need to network with other media houses on issues of the slums, have a more coordinated approach to programme production and presentation at Radio Waumini, develop a workable Kutoka Network media strategy, continuously monitor the listenership and feedback from listeners, as well as training the slum reporters and the programme presenter to improve the quality of slum reporting.
